L0@P0: CLASSICALLY PSH AND PLURIHARMONIC FUNCTIONS ON BERKOVICH SPACES
L1@P0: WALTER GUBLER AND JOSEPH RABINOFF
L2@P0: ABSTRACT. First we extend the theory of subharmonic functions on smooth strictly kanalytic curves from Thuillier’s thesis to the case of possibly singular analytic curves over
L3@P0: a non-archimedean field k. Classically psh functions are then defined as in complex geometry by using pullbacks to analytic curves (and requiring compatibility with base change).
L4@P0: We give various properties of classically psh functions including a local and a global maximum principle. As a consequence, we show that the space of pluriharmonic functions on
L5@P0: a quasi-compact Berkovich space is finite dimensional. As a technical tool, we use that a
L6@P0: connected Berkovich space is connected by analytic curves.
L7@P0: 1. INTRODUCTION
L8@P0: Plurisubharmonic functions are the complex analytic counterparts of subharmonic functions in real analysis. To recall the definition, we begin with the notion of subharmonicity
L9@P0: on the complex line. Let Ω ⊂ C be an open set and let u: Ω → [−∞,∞) be an upper
L10@P0: semicontinuous function. Then u is subharmonic if for every closed ball B(a,r) with center a and radius r contained in Ω and every continuous function h: B(a,r) → R which
L11@P0: is harmonic on the open ball B(a,r) such that u ≤ h on the boundary ∂ B(a,r), we have
L12@P0: u ≤ h on B(a,r). Note that the notion of (sub)harmonicity is insensitive to biholomorphic
L13@P0: maps, hence makes sense on any one-dimensional complex manifold.
L14@P0: Now let X be any complex manifold (without boundary, for simplicity) and let u: X →
L15@P0: [−∞,∞) be an upper semicontinuous function. Then u is plurisubharmonic or psh if,
L16@P0: for every holomorphic map f : B(0, 1) → X from the open unit ball B(0, 1) ⊂ C, the
L17@P0: pullback u ◦ f is subharmonic on B(0, 1). We say that u is pluriharmonic if u and −u are
L18@P0: plurisubharmonic.
L19@P0: Plurisubharmonicity was introduced by Lelong [Lel42] and Oka [Oka42] independently to study holomorphic convexity. It turned out to be a crucial positivity notion
L20@P0: on complex manifolds. Plurisubharmonic functions satisfy the following properties:
L21@P0: (1) The space of psh functions forms a convex cone: that is, if u1, u2 are psh and
L22@P0: λ1,λ2 ≥ 0, then λ1u1 + λ2u2is psh.
L23@P0: (2) If u1, u2 are psh functions then max{u1, u2} is psh.
L24@P0: (3) If {uk}k≥1is a decreasing sequence of psh functions, then u = limukis psh.
L25@P0: (4) A psh function u satisfies the local maximum principle: if u attains a local maximum at x0 ∈ X, then u is constant on the connected component of x0
L26@P0: in X.
L27@P0: 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification. Primary 14G40; Secondary 31C05, 32P05, 32U05.
L28@P0: Key words and phrases. Berkovich spaces, plurisubharmonic and pluriharmonic functions.
L29@P0: W. Gubler was supported by the collaborative research center SFB 1085 Higher Invariants - Interactions
L30@P0: between Arithmetic Geometry and Global Analysis funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft.

L33@P1: Now we consider the non-Archimedean situation. Let k be a field that is complete
L34@P1: with respect to a non-Archimedean absolute value | |. We refer to Section 2 for the
L35@P1: notions used from non-Archimedean geometry. The theory of subharmonic functions
L36@P1: on a smooth, strictly analytic k-curve X has been completely worked out by Thuillier in
L37@P1: his thesis [Thu05]. Thuillier begins by defining harmonic functions as certain piecewise
L38@P1: linear functions satisfying a balancing condition; see [Thu05, §2.3] or 3.2. He then
L39@P1: defines a subharmonic function to be an upper semicontinuous function u: X → R ∪
L40@P1: {−∞} such that, for every strictly affinoid domain U ⊂ X and every harmonic function
L41@P1: h on U such that u ≤ h on ∂ U, we have u ≤ h on U. Thuillier shows that subharmonic
L42@P1: functions on smooth non-Archimedean curves satisfy the properties one would expect,
L43@P1: in analogy to the complex case.
L44@P1: In higher dimensions, it is not completely clear yet what is the best definition for
L45@P1: plurisubharmonic functions. There is the global approach by Zhang [Zha95], who defines a semipositive metric on a line bundle L over a projective k-variety X to be the
L46@P1: uniform limit of metrics induced by nef models. This approach is used in Arakelov geometry for various arithmetic applications. For an ample class θ on X, Boucksom and
L47@P1: Jonsson [BJ22] give a far reaching global pluripotential theory on a projective variety
L48@P1: over a trivially valued field. Some parts work for any non-Archimedean field, at least in
L49@P1: residue characteristic zero. These psh functions might be singular, and the definition uses
L50@P1: decreasing limits of semipositive model functions as in Zhang’s approach. Chambert–Loir
L51@P1: and Ducros [CD25] have posted a second version of their work in which they give a new
L52@P1: definition of psh functions which is functorial and is based on a transfinite regularization
L53@P1: process.
L54@P1: In all of the above approaches, a maximum principle for plurisubharmonic functions
L55@P1: is missing. In this paper, we propose another class of psh functions called classically
L56@P1: plurisubharmonic functions in close analogy to the complex case. The definition is local,
L57@P1: the functions are upper semicontinuous, and we will show that properties (1)–(4) are
L58@P1: satisfied. It will be clear that classically psh functions form a maximal class of reasonable
L59@P1: plurisubharmonic functions that is compatible with Thuillier’s definition for curves. In
L60@P1: particular, the psh functions from the above are classically psh (see 1.2 below).
L61@P1: To get regularization by smooth psh functions in the sense of Chambert-Loir and Ducros
L62@P1: or to define a Monge–Ampère measure for psh functions, additional hypotheses as in
L63@P1: [CD25] might be needed, but that is not the subject of this paper.
L64@P1: 1.1. Subharmonic functions on arbitrary k-analytic curves. In Section 3, we define
L65@P1: subharmonic functions on any k-analytic curve X to be the elements of the following
L66@P1: subsheaf of the sheaf of upper semicontinuous functions on X with range [−∞,∞).
L67@P1: It is the smallest subsheaf that is functorial with respect to pullback, stable under base
L68@P1: change, and agrees with Thuillier’s subharmonic functions on smooth k-analytic curves.
L69@P1: We will show in Proposition 3.5 that subharmonic functions satisfy the properties (1)–(3)
L70@P1: as in the complex case, and the local maximum principle on the interior Int(X) = X \∂ X.
L71@P1: 1.2. Plurisubharmonic functions on k-analytic spaces. We define classically plurisubharmonic functions on k-analytic spaces as the elements of the smallest subsheaf of the
L72@P1-2: sheaf of upper semicontinuous functions with range [−∞,∞) that is functorial withCLASSICALLY PSH AND PLURIHARMONIC FUNCTIONS ON BERKOVICH SPACES 3
L73@P2: respect to pullback, stable under base change, and agrees with the above defined sheaf
L74@P2: of subharmonic functions on k-analytic curves. In Section 4, we will show that classically
L75@P2: psh functions satisfy properties (1)–(3).
L76@P2: We use the terminology classically psh to distinguish from the psh functions introduced
L77@P2: by Chambert-Loir and Ducros in [CD25]. Note that psh functions are classically psh.
L78@P2: Indeed, psh functions are upper semi-continuous and the definition is functorial, so we
L79@P2: are reduced to the case of a smooth analytic curve C. We have to see that a psh function
L80@P2: is subharmonic. By base change, we may assume that k is algebraically closed and nontrivially valued, see Proposition 3.5(7). Since subharmonic functions are stable under
L81@P2: decreasing limits, and the psh functions are defined by a transfinite regularization process
L82@P2: from smooth psh functions, it is enough to show that a smooth psh function on C is
L83@P2: subharmonic. This follows from a result of Wanner [Wan19, Theorem 4.7].
L84@P2: 1.3. Plurisubharmonic R-PL functions. For an R-piecewise linear function h: X → R
L85@P2: on a good strictly k-analytic space over a non-trivially valued field k, we have studied the
L86@P2: notion of semipositivity in the paper [GR25]. This notion is a local analytic version of
L87@P2: the global semipositive metrics introduced by Zhang [Zha95] which are induced by nef
L88@P2: models. We show in Theorem 4.3 that an R-PL function h is semipositive if and only if h
L89@P2: is classically psh.
L90@P2: 1.4. Connectivity by curves. In Theorem 5.4, we show that two points x, y of a connected k-analytic space X can be connected by analytic curves (assumed to be compact
L91@P2: and defined over a non-Archimedean field extension of k). If ∂ X = ;, then we even show
L92@P2: that x, y can be connected by overconvergent curves, which means roughly speaking that
L93@P2: we can connect them with the interiors of compact curves. We refer to Section 5 for the
L94@P2: precise definitions. The proof of Theorem 5.4 is inspired by Berkovich’s proof [Ber90,
L95@P2: §3.2] showing that a connected k-analytic space is pathwise connected. However, we
L96@P2: have to choose different paths, as the ones in ibid are not analytic curves. This result is
L97@P2: related to [dJ95, Proposition 6.1.1] and [Ber07, Theorem 4.1.1] (see the discussion after
L98@P2: the statement of Theorem 5.4 for more details).
L99@P2: Theorem 1.5 (Local Maximum Principle). Let X be a k-analytic space, and let u be a
L100@P2: classically psh function on X. If u has a local maximum on x ∈ Int(X), then u is locally
L101@P2: constant at x.
L102@P2: This will be shown in Theorem 6.1. For the proof, one may assume that ∂ X = ;;
L103@P2: then we reduce the claim to the local maximum principle for k-analytic curves using
L104@P2: connectivity by overconvergent curves.

L106@P2: smallest subset Γ of X such that

L113@P2: has shown that the relative boundary ∂ X is parametrized by analytic spaces defined over
L114@P2-3: non-Archimedean extension fields. An inductive procedure leads us to a stratification of4 W. GUBLER AND J. RABINOFF
L115@P3: ∂ X; we will show in Lemma 6.3 that the minimal strata precisely make up the Shilov
L116@P3: boundary of X. Using this fact, we deduce rather easily the following global maximum
L117@P3: principle from the local maximum principle (Theorem 6.4).
L118@P3: Theorem 1.7. A classically psh function on a k-affinoid space X attains its maximum on
L119@P3: the Shilov boundary of X.
L120@P3: As an application, we will show in Theorem 6.5 that a pointwise limit u of a net of
L121@P3: classically psh functions is classically psh if u is upper semicontinuous.
L122@P3: 1.8. Pluriharmonic functions. As in the complex case, a function u: X → R on the kanalytic space X is called pluriharmonic if u and −u are plurisubharmonic. We study
L123@P3: pluriharmonic functions in Section 7. We will deduce from the above properties of psh
L124@P3: functions that pluriharmonic functions form a sheaf of R-vector spaces, they are closed
L125@P3: under local uniform limits (even pointwise limits if the limit is a continuous real function),
L126@P3: they are stable under base extension and functorial with respect to pullbacks, and they
L127@P3: satisfy the local maximum principle. As a consequence of the global maximum principle
L128@P3: for k-affinoids, we will the following finiteness result in Theorem 7.4.
L129@P3: Theorem 1.9. The set of pluriharmonic functions on a quasicompact k-analytic space is a
L130@P3: finite-dimensional real vector space.
L131@P3: At the end of Section 7, we will see that under certain regularity assumptions on the
L132@P3: k-analytic space X, pluriharmonic functions are R-piecewise linear. We do not know if
L133@P3: this is true without the regularity assumptions.
